name: 12-1 momentum
hypothesis: 12-month return skipping the last month predicts continued outperformance
key_statistic: US WF Sharpe 1.366 for 12-1 vs 1.332 to 1.378 for 2-1 to 9-1; bootstrap P(variant beats 12-1) 46 to 51%; 10-year L/S Sharpe 0.225
note: In the composite. Lookback is a second-order effect; the tilt does not beat equal weight (10-year WF Sharpe 0.966 vs 1.011 for 1/N)

name: Vol-adjusted momentum
hypothesis: 12-month return divided by 63-day realized volatility ranks better than raw momentum
key_statistic: L/S Sharpe -0.060 over 2021 to 2026 in the 9-stock universe
note: In the composite; no standalone evidence that it adds value

name: RSI(14) mean reversion
hypothesis: Oversold names (low RSI) outperform over the next month
key_statistic: Crisis-regime mean-reversion tilt drove +16.86 pp alpha in the COVID 2020 replay; full stack indistinguishable from EW (v2: 1.247 vs 1.272)
note: In the composite; weight 0.05 in risk_on rising to 0.25 in crisis; never tested standalone

name: SMA 50/200 trend
hypothesis: Price above its 50- and 200-day averages predicts continuation
key_statistic: Cross-sectional correlation with 12-1 momentum 0.42; combined-model coefficient flips sign IS (+0.015) to OOS (-0.025)
note: In the composite; overlaps with momentum and breadth; never tested standalone

name: Cross-asset macro
hypothesis: Beta to VIX, yields and oil (US) or rupee, oil and Nifty drawdown by sector (India) should tilt weights toward names that benefit from the macro state
key_statistic: Regime detector as an allocation timer: India 0.435 vs 0.517 buy-and-hold Sharpe; US factor timing 1.220 vs 1.272 EW
note: In the composite. Sub-signals are collinear beta tilts; tested only as part of the stack

name: HRP base weights and the full stack vs equal weight (1/N)
hypothesis: Hierarchical risk parity base weights, and the full signal and risk stack built on them, beat naive equal weight on the same names
key_statistic: Full engine Sharpe 1.247 vs 1.272 for equal weight over 107 monthly periods, bootstrap 95% CI on the difference [-0.13, +0.19]; base weights alone in walk-forward: EW 1.293, inverse vol 1.236, ERC 1.272, HRP 1.243
note: HRP retained as the base of the blend because it does no harm; neither the base weights nor the full stack is distinguishable from 1/N at N=9

name: VIX term structure
hypothesis: VIX/VIX3M backwardation predicts higher forward returns (contrarian)
key_statistic: IS Spearman 0.198, OOS 0.176 (21d SPY); by year 2023 -0.02, 2026 to April -0.50; 0.74 correlation with VIX level
note: Not deployed. Implemented, then removed from the composite as zero-contribution

name: Copper/gold ratio
hypothesis: Falling copper/gold momentum precedes equity gains when VIX is above 15 (contrarian)
key_statistic: WF ICIR 0.355, p 0.0036 (Bonferroni over 14 families p 0.050); L/S Sharpe 0.98 net; crisis ICIR 1.29 on 16 periods
note: Not deployed. Implemented with regime gating, then removed as zero-contribution in the full stack

name: India turn-of-month timing
hypothesis: Rebalancing in the last 3 and first 3 trading days captures a turn-of-month premium
key_statistic: 8.26 bps/day spread, p 0.011 full sample, OOS p 0.013; fails Bonferroni (0.0033)
note: Operational timing rule only; no composite weight; not enforced in code

name: US seasonality composite
hypothesis: Turn-of-month, January, sell-in-May and OpEx-week effects add up to a timing overlay
key_statistic: All p > 0.35; composite IC 0.02 (5d), -0.01 (21d)

name: Put/call ratio (proxies)
hypothesis: Extreme put/call readings are contrarian
key_statistic: No IS significance (p 0.15 to 0.96); non-monotonic quintiles
note: CBOE series unavailable; VIX percentile and SKEW z-score proxies tested instead

name: Insider transactions
hypothesis: Net insider buying predicts returns
key_statistic: 6 purchases in 801 transactions over 2 years; average per-ticker Spearman -0.02
note: Wrong universe and data source

name: Credit spreads (HYG/LQD)
hypothesis: Widening spreads predict lower equity returns
key_statistic: credit_ratio_z 21d IC: IS t -5.48, OOS t +0.59; 5 to 20% annual turnover cost

name: Sector relative strength
hypothesis: Stocks in strong sectors outperform
key_statistic: All 12 OOS correlations flip negative; no IS result survives Bonferroni; all rolling ICIR negative

name: Breadth: share above 50-day SMA
hypothesis: High breadth is contrarian bearish
key_statistic: Raw ICIR -1.45; marginal OOS Spearman 0.00 to -0.03 after controlling for trend and RSI; VIF 4.20
note: Redundant with trend and RSI

name: Breadth: 21-day RSP/SPY momentum
hypothesis: Narrowing breadth predicts higher returns
key_statistic: delta R2 0.0044 IS vs 0.1463 OOS; overlap-adjusted OOS t about 1.84
note: 33x IS-to-OOS increase judged a regime artifact

name: Options skew (CBOE SKEW)
hypothesis: Elevated skew is contrarian bullish
key_statistic: skew_pctile Spearman +0.075 IS, -0.252 OOS; 6.3% annual turnover cost at 5 bps

name: Short interest
hypothesis: High short interest predicts squeezes or informed bearishness
key_statistic: n=9 snapshot only; volume proxy p > 0.2 everywhere
note: No historical series available

name: Variance risk premium
hypothesis: High implied-minus-realized volatility predicts positive returns

name: Bond-equity correlation regime
hypothesis: SPY/TLT correlation z-score predicts returns
key_statistic: 21d IC IS +0.101, OOS -0.136; both significant, opposite signs

name: Earnings revision (analyst actions)
hypothesis: Price-target and rating revisions persist
key_statistic: pt_rev_60d 21d IC IS +0.086, OOS -0.086; action_60d OOS IC 0.100 never walk-forward tested

name: Analyst estimate dispersion
hypothesis: Dispersion is a risk premium or a quality flag
key_statistic: Single cross-section, n=9; dispersion vs 3-month return rho -0.28, p 0.46
note: Cannot be backtested

name: Earnings surprise momentum (PEAD)
hypothesis: Post-earnings-announcement drift persists in mega-caps
key_statistic: Weight 0.00 in all regimes after walk-forward gave zero incremental alpha
note: Removed from the composite; yfinance surprise data sparse for mega-caps

name: INR currency momentum
hypothesis: Rupee weakness helps IT exporters relative to importers
key_statistic: usdinr_z_63d 21d Spearman +0.135 IS, -0.219 OOS; incremental IC after UUP -0.027 (p 0.37)

name: FII/DII flow momentum (INDA proxies)
hypothesis: Foreign flow momentum predicts Nifty
key_statistic: Direct flow: IS IC +0.098, OOS -0.159; INDA/EEM 20d: OOS IC 0.242 but rolling ICIR -0.06; deep dive 4 of 27 tests at 10%, 2.7 expected by chance
note: Never walk-forward validated; not deployed

name: HMM regime detection
hypothesis: A Gaussian HMM detects regimes earlier than VIX thresholds
key_statistic: 3-state model degenerate (risk_on and risk_off alternate daily); 156.5 vs 22.8 transitions per year; WF 179.0% vs 177.1% for the heuristic
note: Research study only; removed from production

name: MOVE/VIX divergence
hypothesis: Bond-equity volatility divergence precedes corrections

name: Momentum lookback variants (2-1 to 9-1)
hypothesis: Shorter lookbacks beat 12-1 in concentrated portfolios
key_statistic: US: no variant beats 12-1 (P 46 to 51%); India: 12-1 best (WF Sharpe 1.232); 5-year 3-1 L/S 0.864 did not reproduce over 10 years (0.158)

name: Sector equal weight
hypothesis: Equal weight across sectors beats naive equal weight
key_statistic: India WF +0.066 Sharpe, CI [-0.121, +0.218]; random sector maps -0.02 to +0.02; US -0.104
note: Acceptable zero-cost default; not an alpha source; the engine uses a sector cap instead

name: Vol targeting (15% US, 20% India)
hypothesis: Scaling exposure to a volatility target improves risk-adjusted return
key_statistic: EW plus overlay vs EW: Sharpe 1.250 vs 1.272 (US), 1.13 vs 1.20 (India); CIs include zero; about 75% average exposure
note: Removed from the engine

name: Factor timing (regime-based cash allocation)
hypothesis: Cut equity to 60% in risk_off and 30% in crisis
key_statistic: Sharpe 1.220 vs 1.272 EW; return -5.96 pp; recovery 389 vs 296 days

name: Sector ETF universe and sector momentum
hypothesis: 10 sector ETFs give a better base and sector momentum works
key_statistic: Sector EW Sharpe 0.654 vs 1.272; sector momentum IC 0.022 (p 0.64)
note: The stock universe is hindsight-selected; the ETF figure is the survivorship-free comparison

name: Crash-buying overlay (leverage or cash buffer)
hypothesis: Add exposure when VIX > 30
key_statistic: Sharpe 1.179 (leverage) and 1.206 (cash buffer) vs 1.272; recovery 75 days vs 296
note: Cash-buffer variant is a risk-preference trade-off, not alpha

name: Country ETF momentum rotation
hypothesis: 12-month momentum across 6 country ETFs
key_statistic: Full-sample Sharpe 0.993 vs WF 0.583; bootstrap difference vs EW CI [-0.67, +1.49]

name: NSE midcap momentum
hypothesis: Momentum works better on less efficient midcaps
key_statistic: EW Sharpe 1.214 vs best momentum 0.964; all bootstrap CIs include zero; removing the top 3 names cuts EW by 0.19

name: Multi-asset regime timing (equity, gold, liquid)
hypothesis: The regime detector times equity vs gold vs cash
key_statistic: Simple detector 0.587 vs 0.517 buy-and-hold, CI [-0.31, +0.45]; full detector 0.435; crisis days followed by +1.16% mean 5-day return

name: Contribution timing on VIX spikes
hypothesis: Double contributions when VIX > 30 or India VIX > 25
key_statistic: US: +0.2% over 30 years vs an equal-capital comparison; India: +10.1% over 18.2 years, two episodes
note: Not implemented; the India result rests on 2008 and 2020
